title: BLASTHub: bulk sequence search on managed NCBI BLAST+ infrastructure
description:
BLASTHub is a web application for bulk sequence similarity search. It executes genuine NCBI BLAST+ searches — blastn, blastp, blastx, tblastn and tblastx — against pre-indexed reference databases on managed cloud infrastructure, and returns the native JSON-15 output parsed into an interactive hit table with per-HSP pairwise alignments.

Nucleotide and protein databases are provided for Drosophila melanogaster, Escherichia coli K-12 MG1655, Saccharomyces cerevisiae S288C and SARS-CoV-2, each pinned to a specific NCBI assembly accession with a recorded SHA-256 checksum and taxonomy identifier. The container build verifies every database with blastdbcmd and runs one search per program before the image ships, so a database that cannot be opened or searched cannot reach production.

Results can be exported as a multi-sheet Excel workbook, a landscape PDF report, or raw JSON and CSV. An optional interpretation step summarises results using the Gemini API; that output is explicitly non-reproducible and is labelled as such in the interface.
notes: Built on the NCBI BLAST+ suite (version 2.17.0), which is a United States Government Work in the public domain. BLAST is a registered trademark of the National Library of Medicine. Reference sequence data is obtained from NCBI RefSeq and remains subject to NCBI data usage policies; accessions and checksums for every bundled database are recorded in docs/DATABASES.md.
